Home.title: Guess the language of the day

description.nasalization: Phonetic feature where some of the sound's air goes through the nose
description.clickConsonants: Strong sounds produced by expelling an enclosed pocket of air
description.tones: The pitch is part of a word's pronunciation and varies between words
description.pitchAccent: A pitch movement or level that marks one syllable in a word as more prominent than the others
description.latinAlphabet: The most used alphabet created by the Romans, most common in Romance languages
description.cyrillicAlphabet: The most common alphabet in the Slavic languages
description.alphabet: Writing system where each grapheme must correspond to a phoneme
description.abjad: Writing system where the vowels are not written, just the consonants
description.abugida: Writing system where the vowels are written as diacritics for the consonants
description.logographic: Writing system that doesn't represent pronunciation but meaning
description.syllabary: Writing system where the symbols correspond to syllable
description.agglutinative: Morphological typology where the morphemes tend to be inflected using affixes
description.fusional: Morphological typology where the morphemes tend to be inflected by modifying the original morpheme
description.isolating: Morphological typology where the morphemes tend to not be inflected, almost a one morpheme per word ratio
description.polysynthetic: Morphological typology with a considerably high morpheme per word ratio
description.ergativeAlignment: Grammatical system where the subject of an intransitive verb is treated like the object of a transitive verb
description.nominativeAccusativeAlignment: Grammatical system where the subject of both transitive and intransitive verbs is treated the same
description.tripartiteAlignment: Grammatical system where the subject of a transitive verb, the object of a transitive verb, and the subject of an intransitive verb are each marked differently
description.svo: Basic word order: Subject Verb Object
description.sov: Basic word order: Subject Object Verb
description.vso: Basic word order: Verb Subject Object
description.vos: Basic word order: Verb Object Subject
description.ovs: Basic word order: Object Verb Subject
description.osv: Basic word order: Object Subject Verb
description.v2: Syntactic rule where the verb has to be the second word of a phrase
description.stressTimed: Phonetic tendency where the stressed syllables take relatively equal intervals, shortening the others
description.syllableTimed: Phonetic tendency where all syllables take relatively equal intervals
description.moraTimed: Small, roughly equal units of timing
description.ejectiveConsonants: Speech sounds produced by closing the vocal tract, trapping air, and then releasing it with a burst using pressure from the glottis rather than from the lungs
description.implosiveConsonants: Speech sounds produced by pulling air inward with a downward movement of the glottis while the oral closure is released
description.retroflexConsonants: Speech sounds produced by curling the tongue tip backwards
description.vowelHarmony: Phonological process where vowels within a word agree in certain features, such as frontness, backness, or rounding
description.nounClasses: Nouns are grouped into categories, often reflected in agreement patterns with adjectives, verbs, or other parts of speech
description.noClasses: Nouns are not grouped into categories or genders
description.dualNumber: The nouns have to be inflected when referring exactly two entities
description.trialNumber: The nouns have to be inflected when referring exactly three entities
description.inclusiveExclusiveWe: Two different pronouns for first person plural, distinguishing between the inclusion or not of the listener
description.evidentiality: Grammatical system that indicates the source or reliability of the speaker’s information, such as whether it was seen, heard, inferred, or reported
description.switchReference: Grammatical system that marks whether the subjects of two linked clauses are the same or different
description.prepositions: The words that indicate relationships between the elements of a sentence are located before the affected noun
description.postpositions: The words that indicate relationships between the elements of a sentence are located after the affected noun
description.noCopula: The verb "to be" (or its equivalent) is often omitted in sentences linking the subject to a predicate, with the relationship implied by context
description.proDrop: The subject of a sentence can be omited with the pronoun implied by conjugation or context
description.focusMarker: Grammatical element that highlights or emphasizes a specific part of a sentence, typically indicating what the speaker considers most important or the focus of the conversation
description.topicMarker: Grammatical element that indicates which part of the sentence is the topic, or what the sentence is about, regardless of its role as subject or object
description.caseMarking: Grammatical system where the function of every noun in a sentence has to be explicit
description.reflexivePronouns: Pronouns that refer back to the subject of the clause, typically used when the subject and the object are the same entity
description.diminutives: Forms of words that convey smallness, affection, or triviality, often created by adding specific affixes or making slight modifications
description.augmentatives: Forms of words that convey strongness or importance often created by adding specific affixes or making slight modifications
description.ideophones: Vivid, often sound-symbolic words that evoke sensory experiences like sounds, movements, colors, or textures
description.classifierSystem: Grammatical system where specific unit particles are used when counting nouns
description.tense: Grammatical category that locates an action or state in time, typically distinguishing past, present, and future
description.aspect: Grammatical category that describes the flow or structure of an action in time, such as whether it is ongoing, completed, habitual, or repetitive
description.mood: Grammatical category that expresses the speaker’s attitude toward the action or state, such as whether it is a command, a wish, a possibility, or a statement of fact
description.personAgreement: Grammatical system where the conjugated verb has to be inflected depending on the grammatical person
description.politenessDistinctions: Grammatical feature where different forms or structures are used to express varying levels of respect, formality, or social distance between speakers
description.consonantClusters: Phonotactics that allow more than 2 consonants to be grouped without vowels (Not silabic consonants)
description.openSyllablesOnly: Phonotactics that only allow sylllables that end in a vowel
description.gemination: The length of the sounds has phonemic value
description.palatalization: Phonological process where a consonant is pronounced closer to the hard palate
description.lateralFricatives: Consonants produced by the friction of the air going through either side of the tongue
description.creakyVoice: Phonation where the vocal cords are tightly compressed and vibrate slowly and irregularly, producing a low, gravelly sound
description.reduplication: The repetition of a morpheme has a grammatical value
description.auxiliaryVerbs: Verbs used alongside a main verb to express grammatical meanings
description.doubleNegation: Construction where two or more negative elements are used in the same clause, often to reinforce or emphasize the negation
description.freeWordOrder: Syntactic feature where the arrangement of words in a sentence is not fixed and can vary without changing the sentence's meaning
description.fixedWordOrder: Syntactic rule where the arrangement of words has an specific order
description.interrogativeParticles: Morphemes used to mark a sentence as a question, often appearing at the beginning or end of a sentence
description.pharyngealization: Phonetic process where a consonant is pronounced with a constriction in the pharynx, giving the sound a distinct "throaty" quality
description.aspiratedConsonants: Consonants that are pronounced with a strong burst of breath
description.labialization: Consonants that are pronounced with an extra labial articulation
